title: RBI intervention bolsters rupee, traders say - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
FILE PHOTO: RBI has rolled out ‌a series of ​measures to address the dollar demand-supply imbalance | Photo Credit: VIVEK PRAKASH

The Reserve Bank ​of India likely intervened in ‌the foreign exchange ​market on ⁠Wednesday, four traders told Reuters, likely to bolster the ‌rupee's recent recovery from near record ‌low levels.

The rupee ‌rose ⁠to 94.95 per ⁠dollar, up about 0.3% from its previous close and ​2% higher ‌on the week so far.

The RBI has rolled out ‌a series of ​measures to address the dollar demand-supply imbalance ⁠that had kept the rupee under sustained ‌pressure. Central bank chief Sanjay Malhotra said on Tuesday that further steps may be taken to ‌ensure orderly movement in the ​currency.

State-run banks were spotted offering dollars ⁠in early trading on Wednesday, ⁠most likely on behalf of ‌the RBI, traders said.
